title: tool_cb_hdr: do not truncate existing file on filename-less C-D header
body:
With -O -J, a Content-Disposition header without a usable filename (for example "inline") made curl create the URL-derived output file right away. When a later Content-Disposition header then named that same file, the no-clobber check refused it, but the file had already been truncated to zero bytes. The same happened when such a header came in a 3xx response before the Location: header with -L.

This defers creating the output file until the body arrives (or the transfer ends), like for any other header. Buffered headers for -i are written at that point.

Tests 1717, 1718 and 1719 cover -OJ, -OJi and -OJL. All three fail without the fix

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="US-ASCII"?>
+<testcase>
+<info>
+<keywords>
+HTTP
+HTTP GET
+-J
+</keywords>
+</info>
+
+<reply>
+<data nocheck="yes">
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Content-Disposition: inline
+Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="name%TESTNUMBER"
+Content-Length: 8
+
+PAYLOAD
+</data>
+<data2 nocheck="yes">
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Content-Disposition: inline
+Content-Length: 0
+
+</data2>
+</reply>
+
+# Client-side
+<client>
+<server>
+http
+</server>
+<name>
+HTTP GET -OJi, filename-less Content-Disposition first
+</name>
+<command option="no-output,no-include">
+http://%HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT/%TESTNUMBER0002 http://%HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT/name%TESTNUMBER -Ji -O -O --output-dir %LOGDIR
+</command>
+<file name="%LOGDIR/name%TESTNUMBER">
+initial content
+</file>
+</client>
+
+# Verify data after the test has been "shot"
+<verify>
+<errorcode>
+23
+</errorcode>
+<file name="%LOGDIR/name%TESTNUMBER">
+initial content
+</file>
+<file2 name="%LOGDIR/%TESTNUMBER0002">
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Content-Disposition: inline
+Content-Length: 0
+
+</file2>
+</verify>
+</testcase>
